topics.label: Lecture Welcome and Context
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the session by framing the significance, complexity, and scope of complement within the broader immunology course.

topics.label: Foundations of Complement and C3 Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the core organizational principles, nomenclature conventions, and central biochemical mechanics of C3 activation.

topics.label: Pathways of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three upstream recognition pathways that drive C3 convertase formation and establish the complement activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream effector mechanisms by which activated complement clears pathogens through opsonization, inflammation, and direct lysis.

topics.label: Host Regulation and Self-Protection Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins prevent host cell destruction by modulating and inactivating complement on host surfaces.

topics.label: Clinical Consequences of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how genetic or acquired deficiencies across different complement proteins produce distinct clinical pathologies.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion Strategies and Applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the evolutionary mechanisms used by pathogens to circumvent complement-mediated destruction and their practical uses in the laboratory.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Outlook
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer closes the session and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
